picks.what: View of the town on its hill above the river, engraving in Cornelis de Bruijn’s Travels into Muscovy
picks.why: only early general view: the town on its hill with churches, the river and the shipyard; plate frame and title trimmed

picks.what: The Mitrofan Monastery at the opening of St. Mitrofan’s relics in 1832, engraving (reproduced on a postcard)
picks.why: the town’s chief landmark, the monastery’s cathedral and bell tower; crowd scene of the 1832 celebration, so marked as an event; postcard caption trimmed

gaps: P0–P1: nothing; P4: only railway stations of other towns (Usman, Kozlov, Putyvl, Dmitriev); P5: only group portraits and 1942 war scenes; P6: existing view kept (#15–#16 show the Don at Storozhevoe, not the city)
notes: #1: drawn during de Bruijn’s 1703 visit, dated by the 1711 first edition of his book per the rules; only 1024 px wide, with the book’s center fold visible. #2: Commons dates the engraving 1839 without a source; it shows the 1832 event and Chesky died in 1848.
